chapters.title: Orchestral exposition
chapters.description: The violins call across a rising sixth. Bassoon and flute answer before the soloist enters.

chapters.title: Solo exposition
chapters.description: The clarinet claims the opening in the middle register; the answering phrase passes briefly to the violins.

chapters.title: Second subject in E
chapters.description: A longer-breathed subject begins on the fifth and folds inward. The clarinet elaborates its cadence.

chapters.title: Development: broken crossings
chapters.description: In F-sharp minor the sixth splits into unanswered calls. The clarinet meets bassoon, flute and viola in smaller combinations.

chapters.title: Dominant and return
chapters.description: The bass stays on E while fragments gather. The return begins in the strings, then yields to the soloist.

chapters.title: Second subject at home
chapters.description: The E-major melody now speaks in A. A passage through the minor subdominant darkens its second half.

chapters.title: Closing ritornello
chapters.description: Solo passagework gives way to a public orchestral cadence; the dominant is left open.

chapters.title: Cadenza
chapters.description: Two unaccompanied paragraphs: the call, an arpeggiated retreat and a winding ascent back to E.

chapters.title: Coda
chapters.description: Clarinet and violins share the closing statement. The orchestra answers with firm, short tonic strokes.

movements.title: II. Adagio cantabile
movements.subtitle: The lamp on the far bank

chapters.title: The lamp
chapters.description: In D major the clarinet stretches the opening sixth across two gentle pulses. Strings leave space around its release.

chapters.title: An answer in low light
chapters.description: Bassoon speaks almost alone; the soloist takes the line below the staff before the flute answers from above.

chapters.title: Through the minor
chapters.description: B minor and its shadow, E minor, carry the tune toward the movement’s orchestral crest.

chapters.title: After the crest
chapters.description: The high note falls away. Viola and bassoon hold the fragments together on the journey home.

chapters.title: Return of the song
chapters.description: The lamp melody comes back with an intimate turn. The following ascent is brighter but quieter than the central climax.

chapters.title: Distant cadence
chapters.description: A brief string memory and a last, low clarinet answer close the song.

chapters.title: Rondo A: the inward step
chapters.description: Three quick notes make the sixth dance. The clarinet leaves holes for short string answers.

chapters.title: B: the reed song
chapters.description: A lilting second idea alternates long and short syllables; a running extension carries it to E.

chapters.title: A, with an answer
chapters.description: The opening solo stays intact as the answer shifts between desks.

chapters.title: C: the wooded bank
chapters.description: F-sharp minor puts the dance lower. Solo bassoon and viola trade its rhythm before a quick upward chase.

chapters.title: A, in close pursuit
chapters.description: The solo rises an octave against a lighter texture. Wind and string desks catch up in relay.

chapters.title: The song behind the dance
chapters.description: The slow movement’s melody is heard in dotted-quarter values, with the dance nearly asleep beneath it.

chapters.title: B renewed
chapters.description: The reed song returns in A: more intimate at first, then doubled back on itself in brighter figuration.

chapters.title: A and the last crossing
chapters.description: The refrain is coloured by the subdominant before it comes home. The soloist and orchestra trade the final call.
